passages.text: One day Samson went down to Timnah, where he saw a young Philistine woman.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man chosen by God.
Samson went down to Timnah.
He saw a woman in Timnah.
She was a daughter of the Philistines.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥רֶד שִׁמְשׁ֖וֹן תִּמְנָ֑תָה וַיַּ֥רְא אִשָּׁ֛ה בְּתִמְנָ֖תָה מִבְּנ֥וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: So he returned and told his father and mother, “I have seen a daughter of the Philistines in Timnah. Now get her for me as a wife.”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man chosen by God.
He went up to his father and mother.
He spoke to them.
He said, “I saw a woman in Timnah.
She is one of the daughters of the Philistines.
Now get her for me as a wife.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֗עַל וַיַּגֵּד֙ לְאָבִ֣יו וּלְאִמּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אִשָּׁ֛ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְתִמְנָ֖תָה מִבְּנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וְעַתָּ֕ה קְחוּ־ אוֹתָ֥הּ לִּ֖י לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: But his father and mother replied, “Can’t you find a young woman among your relatives or among any of our people? Must you go to the uncircumcised Philistines to get a wife?” But Samson told his father, “Get her for me, for she is pleasing to my eyes.”
passages.sermon:
Samson was an Israelite.
His father and mother spoke to him.
They said, “Is there not a woman among your relatives?
Is there not a woman among all our people?
Why do you go to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?”
Samson answered his father.
He said, “Get her for me.
She is right in my eyes.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֜וֹ אָבִ֣יו וְאִמּ֗וֹ הַאֵין֩ בִּבְנ֨וֹת אַחֶ֤יךָ וּבְכָל־ עַמִּי֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֤ה הוֹלֵךְ֙ לָקַ֣חַת אִשָּׁ֔ה מִפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים הָעֲרֵלִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שִׁמְשׁ֤וֹן אֶל־ אָבִיו֙ אוֹתָ֣הּ קַֽח־ לִ֔י כִּֽי־ הִ֖יא יָשְׁרָ֥ה בְעֵינָֽי׃

passages.text: (Now his father and mother did not know this was from the LORD, who was seeking an occasion to move against the Philistines; for at that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.)
passages.sermon:
Samson’s father and mother did not know the truth.
The LORD caused these events.
The LORD wanted to create a reason to act against the Philistines.
At that time, the Philistines ruled over Israel.
passages.original: וְאָבִ֨יו וְאִמּ֜וֹ לֹ֣א יָדְע֗וּ כִּ֤י מֵיְהוָה֙ הִ֔יא כִּי־ תֹאֲנָ֥ה הֽוּא־ מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ מִפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים מֹשְׁלִ֥ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: Then Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother and came to the vineyards of Timnah. Suddenly a young lion came roaring at him, and the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him, and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as one would tear a young goat. But he did not tell his father or mother what he had done.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man chosen by God.
Samson went to Timnah.
His father and mother went with him.
They reached the vineyards of Timnah.
A young lion came toward Samson.
The lion roared at him.
The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon Samson.
Samson tore the lion apart with his bare hands.
He tore the lion as easily as someone tears a young goat.
Samson had nothing in his hands.
Samson did not tell his father what he had done.
Samson did not tell his mother what he had done.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֧רֶד שִׁמְשׁ֛וֹן וְאָבִ֥יו וְאִמּ֖וֹ תִּמְנָ֑תָה וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ עַד־ כַּרְמֵ֣י תִמְנָ֔תָה וְהִנֵּה֙ כְּפִ֣יר אֲרָי֔וֹת שֹׁאֵ֖ג לִקְרָאתֽוֹ׃ וַתִּצְלַ֨ח עָלָ֜יו ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֗ה וַֽיְשַׁסְּעֵ֙הוּ֙ כְּשַׁסַּ֣ע הַגְּדִ֔י וּמְא֖וּמָה אֵ֣ין בְּיָד֑וֹ וְלֹ֤א הִגִּיד֙ לְאָבִ֣יו וּלְאִמּ֔וֹ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃

passages.text: Then Samson continued on his way down and spoke to the woman, because she was pleasing to his eyes.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
Samson went down the road.
Samson spoke to the woman.
The woman pleased Samson.
Samson liked what he saw.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֖רֶד וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר לָאִשָּׁ֑ה וַתִּישַׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י שִׁמְשֽׁוֹן׃

passages.text: When Samson returned later to take her, he left the road to see the lion’s carcass, and in it was a swarm of bees, along with their honey.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man chosen by God.
Samson returned to Timnah after some days.
He came to take the woman he wanted to marry.
He left the road.
He went to look at the dead lion.
He had killed this lion earlier with his bare hands.
He saw something inside the lion’s body.
A swarm of bees was inside the lion’s carcass.
There was honey with the bees.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤שָׁב מִיָּמִים֙ לְקַחְתָּ֔הּ וַיָּ֣סַר לִרְא֔וֹת אֵ֖ת מַפֶּ֣לֶת הָאַרְיֵ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה עֲדַ֧ת דְּבוֹרִ֛ים בִּגְוִיַּ֥ת הָאַרְיֵ֖ה וּדְבָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: So he scooped some honey into his hands and ate it as he went along. And when he returned to his father and mother, he gave some to them and they ate it. But he did not tell them that he had taken the honey from the lion’s carcass.
passages.sermon:
Samson saw a dead lion.
He found a swarm of bees and honey inside the lion’s body.
Samson scooped honey into his hands.
He ate the honey as he walked.
Samson went to his father and mother.
He gave them some of the honey.
They ate the honey.
Samson did not tell his parents where the honey came from.
He did not tell them he took the honey from the lion’s carcass.
passages.original: וַיִּרְדֵּ֣הוּ אֶל־ כַּפָּ֗יו וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הָלוֹךְ֙ וְאָכֹ֔ל וַיֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ אָבִ֣יו וְאֶל־ אִמּ֔וֹ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן לָהֶ֖ם וַיֹּאכֵ֑לוּ וְלֹֽא־ הִגִּ֣יד לָהֶ֔ם כִּ֛י מִגְּוִיַּ֥ת הָאַרְיֵ֖ה רָדָ֥ה הַדְּבָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Then his father went to visit the woman, and Samson prepared a feast there, as was customary for the bridegroom.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man chosen by God.
Samson wanted to marry a woman.
Samson’s father went down to visit the woman.
Samson prepared a feast at that place.
It was the custom for a bridegroom to make a feast.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥רֶד אָבִ֖יהוּ אֶל־ הָאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיַּ֨עַשׂ שָׁ֤ם שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה כִּ֛י כֵּ֥ן יַעֲשׂ֖וּ הַבַּחוּרִֽים׃

passages.text: And when the Philistines saw him, they selected thirty men to accompany him.
passages.sermon: The Philistines saw Samson.\r\nThey chose thirty men.\r\nThese thirty men stayed with Samson.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֖י כִּרְאוֹתָ֣ם אוֹת֑וֹ וַיִּקְחוּ֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים מֵֽרֵעִ֔ים וַיִּהְי֖וּ אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “Let me tell you a riddle,” Samson said to them. “If you can solve it for me within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a strong man and a judge of Israel.
Samson spoke to the thirty Philistine men.
Samson said, “Let me tell you a riddle.”
Samson said, “If you solve my riddle during the seven days of the wedding feast, I will give you thirty linen garments.”
Samson said, “I will also give you thirty sets of clothes.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן אָחֽוּדָה־ נָּ֥א לָכֶ֖ם חִידָ֑ה אִם־ הַגֵּ֣ד תַּגִּידוּ֩ אוֹתָ֨הּ לִ֜י שִׁבְעַ֨ת יְמֵ֤י הַמִּשְׁתֶּה֙ וּמְצָאתֶ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֤י לָכֶם֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים סְדִינִ֔ים וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים חֲלִפֹ֥ת בְּגָדִֽים׃

passages.text: But if you cannot solve it, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.” “Tell us your riddle,” they replied. “Let us hear it.”
passages.sermon:
Samson spoke to the thirty Philistine men.
He said, "If you cannot solve my riddle, you must give me thirty linen garments."
He also said, "You must give me thirty sets of clothes."
The men replied to Samson.
They said, "Tell us your riddle."
They said, "Let us hear it."
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹ֣א תוּכְלוּ֮ לְהַגִּ֣יד לִי֒ וּנְתַתֶּ֨ם אַתֶּ֥ם לִי֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים סְדִינִ֔ים וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים חֲלִיפ֣וֹת בְּגָדִ֑ים וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ ח֥וּדָה חִידָתְךָ֖ וְנִשְׁמָעֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: So he said to them: “Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet.” For three days they were unable to explain the riddle.
passages.sermon:
Samson spoke to the men at the feast.
He gave them a riddle.
He said, “Out of the eater came something to eat.
Out of the strong came something sweet.”
The men could not solve the riddle for three days.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם מֵהָֽאֹכֵל֙ יָצָ֣א מַאֲכָ֔ל וּמֵעַ֖ז יָצָ֣א מָת֑וֹק וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֛וּ לְהַגִּ֥יד הַחִידָ֖ה שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: So on the fourth day they said to Samson’s wife, “Entice your husband to explain the riddle to us, or we will burn you and your father’s household to death. Did you invite us here to rob us?”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
Samson gave a riddle to the Philistines at his wedding feast.
On the seventh day, the men of the city spoke to Samson’s wife.
They said, “Persuade your husband to tell us the answer to the riddle.”
They threatened her.
They said, “If you do not, we will burn you and your father’s house with fire.”
They accused her.
They said, “Did you invite us here to take what belongs to us?”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ לְאֵֽשֶׁת־ שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ פַּתִּ֣י אֶת־ אִישֵׁ֗ךְ וְיַגֶּד־ לָ֙נוּ֙ אֶת־ הַ֣חִידָ֔ה פֶּן־ נִשְׂרֹ֥ף אוֹתָ֛ךְ וְאֶת־ בֵּ֥ית אָבִ֖יךְ בָּאֵ֑שׁ הַלְיָרְשֵׁ֕נוּ קְרָאתֶ֥ם לָ֖נוּ הֲלֹֽא׃

passages.text: Then Samson’s wife came to him, weeping, and said, “You hate me! You do not really love me! You have posed to my people a riddle, but have not explained it to me.” “Look,” he said, “I have not even explained it to my father or mother, so why should I explain it to you?”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man chosen by God.
Samson had a wife from the Philistines.
Samson’s wife came to him.
She wept before him.
She said, “You hate me.”
She said, “You do not love me.”
She said, “You gave a riddle to my people.”
She said, “You did not tell me the answer.”
Samson answered her.
He said, “I have not told my father.”
He said, “I have not told my mother.”
He said, “Why should I tell you?”
passages.original: וַתֵּבְךְּ֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת שִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן עָלָ֗יו וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ רַק־ שְׂנֵאתַ֙נִי֙ וְלֹ֣א אֲהַבְתָּ֔נִי הַֽחִידָ֥ה חַ֙דְתָּ֙ לִבְנֵ֣י עַמִּ֔י וְלִ֖י לֹ֣א הִגַּ֑דְתָּה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֗הּ הִנֵּ֨ה לְאָבִ֧י וּלְאִמִּ֛י לֹ֥א הִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְלָ֥ךְ אַגִּֽיד׃

passages.text: She wept the whole seven days of the feast, and finally on the seventh day, because she had pressed him so much, he told her the answer. And in turn she explained the riddle to her people.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
Samson had a wife from the Philistines.
There was a wedding feast that lasted seven days.
Samson’s wife cried during all seven days of the feast.
She wept because she wanted Samson to tell her the answer to his riddle.
She pressed him every day.
On the seventh day, Samson told her the answer.
He told her because she had pressed him so much.
Samson’s wife then told the answer to her people.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֤בְךְּ עָלָיו֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ הָיָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם הַמִּשְׁתֶּ֑ה וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וַיַּגֶּד־ לָהּ֙ כִּ֣י הֱצִיקַ֔תְהוּ וַתַּגֵּ֥ד הַחִידָ֖ה לִבְנֵ֥י עַמָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Before sunset on the seventh day, the men of the city said to Samson: “What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?” So he said to them: “If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have solved my riddle!”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
He was strong.
He gave a riddle to the men of the city.
The men of the city wanted to solve the riddle.
On the seventh day, before sunset, the men of the city spoke to Samson.
They said, “What is sweeter than honey?”
They said, “What is stronger than a lion?”
Samson answered them.
He said, “If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have solved my riddle.”
Samson meant they learned the answer by using his wife.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לוֹ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י הָעִ֜יר בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י בְּטֶ֙רֶם֙ יָבֹ֣א הַחַ֔רְסָה מַה־ מָּת֣וֹק מִדְּבַ֔שׁ וּמֶ֥ה עַ֖ז מֵאֲרִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם לוּלֵא֙ חֲרַשְׁתֶּ֣ם בְּעֶגְלָתִ֔י לֹ֥א מְצָאתֶ֖ם חִידָתִֽי׃

passages.text: Then the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon, killed thirty of their men, took their apparel, and gave their clothes to those who had solved the riddle. And burning with anger, Samson returned to his father’s house, and his wife was given to one of the men who had accompanied him.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man chosen by God.
The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon Samson.
Samson went down to the city of Ashkelon.
Samson killed thirty men in Ashkelon.
Samson took the clothes from the thirty men.
Samson gave these clothes to the men who had solved his riddle.
Samson became very angry.
Samson returned to his father’s house.
Samson’s wife was given to one of the men who had been his companion.
passages.original: וַתִּצְלַ֨ח עָלָ֜יו ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֗ה וַיֵּ֨רֶד אַשְׁקְל֜וֹן וַיַּ֥ךְ מֵהֶ֣ם׀ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים אִ֗ישׁ וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־ חֲלִ֣יצוֹתָ֔ם וַיִּתֵּן֙ הַחֲלִיפ֔וֹת לְמַגִּידֵ֖י הַחִידָ֑ה וַיִּ֣חַר אַפּ֔וֹ וַיַּ֖עַל בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיהוּ׃פ וַתְּהִ֖י אֵ֣שֶׁת שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן לְמֵ֣רֵעֵ֔הוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר רֵעָ֖ה לֽוֹ׃
